title: Field extension of the subgroup generated by a pointed affine morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $K/k$ any field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $X$ be an affine $k$-scheme of finite type, let $o\in X(k)$ be a $k$-rational point [def-pc-rational-point], and let $\varphi:X\to G$ be a $k$-morphism with $\varphi(o)=e$. Suppose that for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the subset $\varphi(X(R))\subseteq G(R)$ is stable under inversion. Let $L\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] through which $\varphi$ factors, and suppose $L$ is smallest with this property: for every closed subgroup scheme $H\subseteq G$ through which $\varphi$ factors, $L\subseteq H$. Write $G_K$, $X_K$, $L_K$ and $\varphi_K$ for scalar extensions [def-pc-base-change]. Then $L_K$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $G_K$, the morphism $\varphi_K$ factors through $L_K$, and for every closed subgroup scheme $H\subseteq G_K$ through which $\varphi_K$ factors one has $L_K\subseteq H$. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness, or algebraicity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, printed p.55, in the affine pointed-map setting of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ put $A=k[G]$, $B_n=k[X^n]$, $I_n=\ker(w_n^*:A\to B_n)$ and $I=\bigcap_nI_n$, where $w_n$ multiplies the $n$ images under $\varphi$. By [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup], $L'=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is the smallest closed subgroup through which $\varphi$ factors: all its hypotheses are precisely those of the item. Minimality in both directions identifies $L=L'$ as closed subschemes of $G$. Write $C=A/I$ and $q:A\to C$. Since $I\subseteq I_n$, define $f_n:C\to B_n$ by $f_n(q(a))=w_n^*(a)$. If every $f_n(q(a))$ vanishes, $a\in I$, hence $q(a)=0$; thus the $f_n$ jointly detect zero.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, printed p.55, using the affine construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], set $A_K=A\otimes_kK$, $C_K=C\otimes_kK$, $B_{n,K}=B_n\otimes_kK$: these are the coordinate rings of $G_K,L_K,(X^n)_K$. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] and functoriality of [def-pc-base-change] identify $(X^n)_K=(X_K)^n$ and the word-map pullback with $(f_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_K)\circ(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_K)$; this equality holds on each $a\otimes\lambda$. The map $q_K=q\otimes\mathrm{id}_K:A_K\to C_K$ is surjective: lift each coefficient in a finite tensor sum to $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $L_K\to G_K$ is closed. For every $K$-algebra $R$, its points identify with $L(R)\subseteq G(R)$, so [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] makes it a closed subgroup. Base-changing the given factorization gives $\varphi_K:X_K\to L_K\to G_K$.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, printed p.55, using the affine construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] with $M=C$, $N=K$, index set the positive integers, $P_n=B_n$ and maps $f_n$. Its joint-zero-detection hypothesis was proved in step 1; all objects are $k$-vector spaces. It follows that for $t\in C_K$, if $(f_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_K)(t)=0$ for every $n\geq1$, then $t=0$. This treats the whole infinite family, without any stabilization or finite-dimensionality assumption.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, printed p.55, using the affine construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Let $H\subseteq G_K$ be a closed subgroup through which $\varphi_K$ factors. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $H=\operatorname{Spec}(A_K/J)$. Its subgroup multiplication [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] makes each word map $(X_K)^n\to G_K$ factor through $H$. Thus for $a\in J$, every $(f_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_K)(q_K(a))$ vanishes; step 3 implies $q_K(a)=0$. The formula $a+J\mapsto q_K(a)$ therefore defines a surjective map $A_K/J\to C_K$, since $q_K$ is surjective. Contravariance of affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] give a closed immersion $L_K\to H$ over $G_K$. Hence $L_K\subseteq H$, proving the required minimality.
